turns.text: Turn the clock back to 2006. What problem was SURF actually trying to solve?

Herbert Bay, Tinne Tuytelaars, and Luc Van Gool introduced SURF as a faster scale- and rotation-invariant local feature detector and descriptor. It used integral images and approximated Hessian responses to make robust matching more efficient.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?
Integral images speed up box-filter responses, then stable interest points receive compact descriptors.
Why did the idea outlive one paper or experiment? What did later researchers actually inherit?

Experts generally treat SURF as an important engineering advance in pre-deep-learning local features. Its long-term legacy is the emphasis on robust matching that is fast enough for practical image retrieval, stitching, and robotics pipelines.
SURF mattered not only as a result, but as a method that later researchers could test, adapt, and extend.
